title: The pDAI stabilization thesis - main report
text:
The pDAI stabilization thesis
4 October 2026. Research white paper. Blockchain investigation is read-only. Contract observations
retain their dated checkpoints.
Purpose and scope
The sole intended purpose of this report is to observe, document and interpret activity on
PulseChain. It does not provide financial, investment, trading, legal, tax or any other advice.
It does not recommend buying, selling, lending, staking or otherwise using any asset, protocol or
proposed route. References to a $1 target, financing, arbitrage, governance changes and possible
outcomes are observational research hypotheses, not price forecasts, guarantees or instructions to act.
Evidence and interpretations retain their dated checkpoints and stated assumptions. This purpose
applies to the entire report, its historical appendices and its supporting files.
The thesis
This paper examines a proposed reconstruction of PulseChain's inherited financial
infrastructure around pDAI. Its working assumption is coordinated intent to benefit pDAI and
PulseChain. Under that assumption, governance changes, receipt issuance, stablecoin conversions and
distributed arbitrage serve complementary purposes: mobilize capital, manage supply, build usable
liquidity and finance continued support.
The strategy combines private-L2 funding or instructions with permitted local operations. Existing token
addresses preserve connections to existing markets; credit can separate initial financing from later
settlement; gradual purchases build positions; target-price sales return pDAI to circulation and recover
payment capital; outside activity can generate income for replenishment. A funded two-sided pDAI dollar
policy is the service this network aims to deliver. Its corrective rule is to buy below the target, meet
demand with target-price offers, and restore the inputs consumed; an independent executable dollar
reference determines payment amounts.
Its comparison rule is one normalized eligible pStable = one accounting unit, U. Receipts and LP
shares first convert to their underlying claim values. Common U directs relative arbitrage; a $1 policy
additionally selects payment quantities tied to an independently executable dollar value.
Capital and execution can span apparently unrelated wallets and productive positions, with spendable
inputs arriving when needed. A central treasury, visible accumulator or persistent local stockpile is not
assumed.

1. Why pDAI could organize the restored network
pDAI is useful in this construction because several paths already meet at its exact local identity. It is a
3pool base coin, FEI's conversion asset, the input to a registered Synthetix DAI wrapper, and the output
of remaining Maker savings-credit conversion. Aave receipts and native-token markets add further
connections. The route evidence (Appendix 35) records these distinct paths; ordinary Maker PSM
conversion is shut down.
The proposed strategic choice is to make pDAI a commonly used settlement and pricing asset across
those paths. Acquiring it provides potential sale inventory and inputs for compatible conversions. pUSDC
and pUSDT remain important companion assets for base-pool liquidity and routing. The evidence
establishes connections; choosing pDAI as the organizing asset is the thesis, rather than a consequence
of pool membership alone.

These are complementary roles and alternative branches. A useful subset can operate the strategy. The 
network map (Appendix 37) and issuer audit (Appendix 38) retain the token and authority details;
common control of every issuer is not a premise established by this research.
2. How capital reaches the local markets
Every selected route must perform five jobs: source funding, destination acceptance, funded
conversion, price-sensitive trading, and replenishment.

Private L2 asset or receipt OR permitted local financing
                         ↓ accepted delivery or local issuance
Existing local pool coin OR accepted aToken/wrapper
                         ↓ funded issuer / Curve / Balancer / other market
pDAI, neighboring stablecoins or PLS across participating wallets
                         ↓ gradual purchases and liquidity allocation
Usable inputs for bids, offers and connected-market conversions

Restored capacity and settled obligations
Authorized L2 instructions can coordinate local execution separately.
Destination route Required connection
Direct delivery The bridge returns the exact token already accepted by a
local issuer or market; escrow, minter or relayer funding
permits delivery.
Receipt adaptation A representation enters a compatible local issuer, which
values it and creates its existing pool coin.
Source and destination addresses need not match. The final accepted local token matters. One proposed
receipt route is L2 vault receipt → authenticated representation → Reserve collateral plugin
and active basket → existing Reserve eUSD → eUSD/FRAXBP → funded pUSDC → pDAI or PLS
conversion. Plugin registration, basket selection, refresh, pricing and issuance must work. Existing
basket components cannot simply be replaced by supplying one new token.
Origin OUSD and mUSD connect through 3CRV and have different collateral rules. Existing accepted
inputs may avoid changes; a new receipt needs compatible onboarding or an upgrade. Direct delivery of
existing pDAI can supply offers or eligible reserves without an issuer detour. FEI and Synthetix
conversions are optional branches when they improve net output or distribution. FEI receives a worked
example because its local one-for-one conversion is clearly demonstrated; it links FEI to pDAI units,
rather than independently anchoring either to dollars. The saved Synthetix evidence also connects
native PLS purchases of pDAI, wrapper issuance of sUSD and funded market outputs; these mixed-
position flows are not one isolated profitable cycle or fresh L2 delivery.
Each arrow needs its asset, effective executor, payer, obligations and timing. Attestations authenticate
state or delivery; issuance creates claims; a funded market supplies the paid asset. A successful local
cycle validates local circulation. Fresh L2 financing additionally needs its accepted delivery and source
obligations; instructions can coordinate spending without supplying assets. Copied Arbitrum authority
does not confer Optimism/Synthetix permissions. The control audit (Appendix 52) preserves those
distinctions.
3. Aave and Portal can advance local claims
Aave is the lending and receipt layer; Portal is its V3 destination-credit branch. Ordinary
supply deposits underlying and creates its aT oken. Borrowing draws available reserve cash and creates
debt. Portal lets an authorized Bridge caller issue the recognized destination aT oken before matching
underlying arrives. Source authentication belongs to the adapter; Aave checks local permission and
reserve validation. This is the credit concept in Aave's Portal proposal.

This branch separates early financing from later backing. Selling compatible receipts obtains market
assets; matching-receipt repayment can remove debt-based withdrawal constraints when account

The liquidity index changes receipt accounting rather than multiplying new principal: issuing 100 current

receipts. The wrapper census (Appendix 24) identifies V3 DAI/USDC/USDT/WETH wrappers and 17 direct
Aave linear pools across V2 and V3.
At the saved checkpoints, all 17 unbacked caps were zero. Activation needs Bridge permission, positive
allowance, ordinary supply headroom, compatible wrappers and funded output markets. These are
specific implementation milestones; raising one cap is insufficient. The Portal audit (Appendix 48) retains
the gates and authority requirements. The timing and settlement policy appear below.

5. Common accounting directs connected market
arbitrage
The policy admits specific tokens, normalizations, conversion rights, limits and suspension conditions.
Common U compares opportunities; actual fees, basket rules, slippage and available payment assets
determine execution. Funded conversions transmit support through the eligible connected markets in
each usable direction. Fees, capacity and delays determine the achievable relative-price bands; one
working mint does not establish the reverse route or every AMM quote.
Buy a cheap eligible coin, convert through an accepting issuer and obtain a coin scarce elsewhere. Or
buy a cheap issuer coin and redeem its funded underlying. Authorized issuance or removal of supply can
extend those operations. Under the restoration interpretation, the objective is to improve connected
liquidity while acquiring useful assets; each individual trade need not profit.
Curve connects OUSD, mUSD and other metacoins to pDAI/pUSDC/pUSDT through 3CRV; Reserve eUSD
uses FRAXBP . Balancer and lending venues provide further eligible paths. Shared base reserves count
once: multiple issuer routes using the same 3pool or FRAXBP cash are not independently funded
alternatives. Rebalancing one venue must account for the payment resources and obligations left in the
others. Selling newly issued tokens into a pool consumes counterassets; reverse trades, funded
redemption or contraction, or new inputs must restore the needed capacity.
FEI has a demonstrated one-for-one pDAI conversion. Historical mUSD and post-shutdown sDAI cycles
closed with 200,053.199510 PLS and 110.687385 PLS after gas. These usable proceeds could
finance later operations; their subsequent deployment is a separate connection to establish. Profit and
direct price support are distinct jobs: the actual sDAI cycle ended by selling pDAI and slightly lowering its
closing pool's PLS/pDAI ratio. Under coordinated intent, its proceeds could support a different venue. The
policy must assess complete closing flows. The closed-trade reconciliation (Appendix 25) records the
actual endpoints.
Supply buffers differ by implementation. The checked PWRD/STBT pools use live balances; OUSD, UZD
and Lybra have different treatment. Rebases, minting, borrowing and income require separate resource
accounting. The rebase audit (Appendix 36) preserves these distinctions.
6. Build support gradually and keep pDAI circulating
The proposed construction has five phases. They can overlap; selected routes become usable before the
whole network is commissioned.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 9

Phase Proposed action and observable milestone
Activate routes Establish effective permissions, compatible token behavior,
accepted collateral and funded conversions.
Accumulate gradually Repeated purchases build useful pDAI and neighboring-
stable positions across wallets and protocols.
Build execution depth Fund appropriate pool sides and conversion markets;
measure paid output at the supported sizes.
Operate the price policy Deliver timely purchases and sales at quantities tied to the
chosen dollar reference; recover payment resources and
route pDAI into measured reserve shortages.
Extend economic use Enable usable entry, spending, borrowing and exits;
reinvest attributable net income into continued support.
The acquisition assumption is a consistent allocation every ten seconds while pDAI is below target and
the route is funded. The 50bn allocation enters over time. At 8,640 daily slots, 10,000 input-token units
per slot takes about 579 days to deploy 50bn; 1,000 takes about 16 years, before pauses. Input units
are not verified dollars. Splitting orders reduces individual impact; total impact still depends on
replenishment and market depth.
Acquiring a finite seller cohort can reduce its remaining inventory. Liquidity allocation and lending can
also return pDAI to circulation through purchases, withdrawals and borrow-and-sell activity. The strategy
therefore needs circulation rules, rather than treating acquired supply as permanently unavailable.
Operating decision Required specification
Reference and payment Independently executable dollar valuation and exact
funded payment asset.
Execution Supported sizes, all-in bid/offer band and settlement
deadline.
Capacity Cumulative flows, source outages and reference/liquidity
shocks covered.
Replenishment Incoming assets, opposite trades, withdrawals or net
earnings, with delivery deadlines and obligations counted
once.
If eligible holders can reach funded bids and offers at the declared net terms, sizes and deadlines, those
completed orders receive the declared band. This is the conditional deterministic result. It concerns the
accessible funded service, including routes through LPs, rather than every finite pool's standalone quote.
Receipt surplus or dominant ownership alone does not supply its premises.
The appendix proposes 1,000-pDAI orders within an all-in ±1% band over 24 hours, with declared flow
limits and an Ethereum-origin USDC payment candidate. This is a research benchmark, not an observed
operator promise. Copied $1 oracle marks do not establish the payment's dollar value. PLS, ETH or BTC
can provide variable-price payment assets if quantities track an independent executable reference.
Target-price sales are the replenishment phase of the acquisition strategy. Buyers receive pDAI
while the network receives payment assets that can fund subsequent support. The policy also routes
available pDAI into measured shortages across connected pools, lending reserves and compatible
issuers. Releasing supply at the target can serve demand and contain a premium while restoring useful
circulation.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 10

A funded offer at the target also creates a distribution incentive: where another venue pays a premium
on the same executable valuation basis, traders can buy pDAI at the target and sell it into that venue,
narrowing the premium if the spread covers costs. This lets outside arbitrage participate in the refill.
Acquired or validly issued pDAI available through permitted positions
                  ├─ target-price sale to users → payment capital recovers
                  ├─ routed sale into 3pool → DAI reserve rises; output asset falls
                  ├─ 3pool liquidity deposit → DAI reserve rises; 3CRV is issued
                  └─ compatible lending/issuer supply → its pDAI cash rises
Recovered payment assets + new capital + collectible net earnings
                              ↓
                    further support and replenishment
Here, 3pool holds pDAI/pUSDC/pUSDT; 3CRV is its LP token. A routed pDAI sale into 3pool restores its
DAI side by withdrawing another base asset. A pDAI liquidity deposit adds DAI and obtains 3CRV under
the pool's rules; those claims can connect to accepting metapools. These exchange/deposit directions
follow Curve's 3pool logic; the local token identities retain their saved checkpoints. The network must
budget the other base assets and shared reserves alongside the pDAI refill.
A direct sale to a user restores the seller's payment resources. Its further allocation determines which
pool or lending reserve is refilled. Conversely, a user buying pDAI from 3pool removes DAI while adding
the input stablecoin. The proposed network closes that loop by supplying pDAI where routed demand
removes it and directing recovered resources to the next support requirement. The aim is repeated
redistribution across the ecosystem, with each shortage and funded refill recorded.
The sampled Aave DAI reserve had zero pDAI cash. A valid ordinary supply can add cash while creating
its aT oken claim, making that refill a measurable destination objective. It does not clear separate Portal
principal. Gross sale proceeds recycle capital; only realized net margins or fees count as income.
Proceeds allocated to backing, earning positions or other venues also compete with payment capacity
for recirculated pDAI. One shared resource-and-deadline budget must cover the chosen commitments
across wallets. Renewed selling still requires timely inputs, and lending can return pDAI through
withdrawals or borrow-and-sell activity. More aT okens than pT okens provides support through permitted
funded conversions. V2 execution changes with size; a price touch does not specify a lasting service.
Universal fixed Ethereum redemption is not required for the bounded local policy. External access still
needs valid representations and funded paths. Proposed Ethereum pDAI/ETH or pDAI/WBTC LPs have
variable exchange rates and require separate deployment, reserves and bridge evidence.

These separate clocks explain the proposed long preparation and accumulation period. A funded relayer
can advance destination assets before reimbursement. Portal exposure can persist for years in state,
consuming capacity while withdrawals need cash. Integration terms can impose deadlines and fees.
Eventual backUnbacked requires an authorized Bridge caller, matching underlying, allowance and supplied
fee. Ordinary supply or borrower debt repayment does not clear this principal. The deferred-financing
study (Appendix 34) retains all twelve examined debts and the settlement rules.
The favorable feedback is:
Gradual acquisitions + funded liquidity
                   ↓
More reliable exchange and useful credit
                   ↓ possible adoption
Outside payments, trading and borrowing
                   ↓ collectible net income
Reinvestment + incoming capital + target-price sales
                   ↓
Timely support inputs and eventual backing
                   ↺ restored capacity
The proposed reinvestment policy directs all attributable net earnings to support after costs, losses and
required obligations. Outside trading fees, paid borrower interest and realized rewards can contribute
when the network owns the entitlement. Fees between controlled accounts cancel; principal and gross
turnover are not income. LP shares sent to an inaccessible burn address provide no usable fee
entitlement; ordinary liquidity withdrawal burns shares while returning assets under the pool's rules.
Pledged collateral cannot also be free payment capacity, and nested receipts count the same underlying
once.
PLS/HEX/PLSX/INC positions need actual entitlement and realizable proceeds. Direct native collateral in
Origin or Reserve requires compatible strategies/plugins and valuation; proceeds can instead buy
existing accepted collateral. Funding can remain in productive positions and arrive just in time for
execution.
The accumulation study (Appendix 65) explains the feedback. The liquidity-growth study (Appendix 40)
models depth and reinvestment under explicit hypothetical inputs. Neither establishes actual future
demand or income. As parity improves, arbitrage spreads can shrink; perpetual arbitrage profit is not
required. Recycled capital, opposite flows, new funded inputs and collectible net income can maintain
the service within its budget. Retiring 86ff's debt also removes its future interest contribution; the plan
cannot count future interest from that retired debt. Saved gates—zero Portal caps, broken sETH2 logic,
disabled ordinary Maker PSM and finite issuer cash—identify the changes or alternative routes needed
before their capacity contributes.

8. Define the benefit to PulseChain participants
The proposed public benefit is reliable exchange and productive use across the network. Acquisition and
permissions serve that outcome. Its success measures differ by participant:
Participant Proposed benefit and measurement
pDAI holders Reliable execution: paid output, supported size, costs and
waiting time.
Borrowers Usable credit: available reserve cash, debt terms,
repayment and withdrawal rights.
Liquidity providers Attributable outside fees alongside inventory risk, losses
and withdrawal access.
Stablecoin users and issuers Working conversions, pDAI replenishment into measured
shortages, balanced resources and reconciled redemption
claims.
Native-asset participants Additional productive use, realized rewards or funded
demand; native appreciation is not assumed.
New users Usable entry, settlement and exit paths at actual costs and
sizes.
Moving resources between venues can finance a broader reconstruction. Its benefit must appear in the
resulting depth, claims, coverage and access of affected participants; changing one group's position
does not establish a gain for every holder.
The canonical PulseChain–Ethereum bridge is the external-capital boundary for this interpretation.
Copied Across and private-L2 gateways are separate objects. A proposed supporting observation is rising
PLS per pDAI and persistent canonical bridge assets over three years while PLS declines; a matched time
series remains to be reconstructed.
Stable asset quantities despite completed releases require offsetting inputs or reconciled changes.
Stable dollar TVL alone can reflect revaluation. Replacement inflows may restore backing while creating
replacement claims. The useful pattern to measure is capital arrival followed by distributed net
acquisition, usable liquidity, economic activity and replenishment. PLS privacy may obscure lineage, but
active deployment and relevant use remain unverified. The intent assessment (Appendix 28) retains
independent inflow, recycling and other explanations; persistent vulnerable code alone does not imply
inevitable zero value.

The pDAI stabilization thesis
4 October 2026. Research white paper. Blockchain investigation is read-only. Contract observations
retain their dated checkpoints.
Purpose and scope
The sole intended purpose of this report is to observe, document and interpret activity on
PulseChain. It does not provide financial, investment, trading, legal, tax or any other advice.
It does not recommend buying, selling, lending, staking or otherwise using any asset, protocol or
proposed route. References to a $1 target, financing, arbitrage, governance changes and possible
outcomes are observational research hypotheses, not price forecasts, guarantees or instructions to act.
Evidence and interpretations retain their dated checkpoints and stated assumptions. This purpose
applies to the entire report, its historical appendices and its supporting files.
The thesis
This paper examines a proposed reconstruction of PulseChain's inherited financial
infrastructure around pDAI. Its working assumption is coordinated intent to benefit pDAI and
PulseChain. Under that assumption, governance changes, receipt issuance, stablecoin conversions and
distributed arbitrage serve complementary purposes: mobilize capital, manage supply, build usable
liquidity and finance continued support.
The strategy combines private-L2 funding or instructions with permitted local operations. Existing token
addresses preserve connections to existing markets; credit can separate initial financing from later
settlement; gradual purchases build positions; target-price sales return pDAI to circulation and recover
payment capital; outside activity can generate income for replenishment. A funded two-sided pDAI dollar
policy is the service this network aims to deliver. Its corrective rule is to buy below the target, meet
demand with target-price offers, and restore the inputs consumed; an independent executable dollar
reference determines payment amounts.
Its comparison rule is one normalized eligible pStable = one accounting unit, U. Receipts and LP
shares first convert to their underlying claim values. Common U directs relative arbitrage; a $1 policy
additionally selects payment quantities tied to an independently executable dollar value.
Capital and execution can span apparently unrelated wallets and productive positions, with spendable
inputs arriving when needed. A central treasury, visible accumulator or persistent local stockpile is not
assumed.

and two profitable closed trades at saved checkpoints.

1. Why pDAI could organize the restored network
pDAI is useful in this construction because several paths already meet at its exact local identity. It is a
3pool base coin, FEI's conversion asset, the input to a registered Synthetix DAI wrapper, and the output
of remaining Maker savings-credit conversion. Aave receipts and native-token markets add further
connections. The route evidence (Appendix 35) records these distinct paths; ordinary Maker PSM
conversion is shut down.
The proposed strategic choice is to make pDAI a commonly used settlement and pricing asset across
those paths. Acquiring it provides potential sale inventory and inputs for compatible conversions. pUSDC
and pUSDT remain important companion assets for base-pool liquidity and routing. The evidence
establishes connections; choosing pDAI as the organizing asset is the thesis, rather than a consequence
of pool membership alone.

2. How capital reaches the local markets
Every selected route must perform five jobs: source funding, destination acceptance, funded
conversion, price-sensitive trading, and replenishment.

Source and destination addresses need not match. The final accepted local token matters. One proposed
receipt route is L2 vault receipt → authenticated representation → Reserve collateral plugin
and active basket → existing Reserve eUSD → eUSD/FRAXBP → funded pUSDC → pDAI or PLS
conversion. Plugin registration, basket selection, refresh, pricing and issuance must work. Existing

Origin OUSD and mUSD connect through 3CRV and have different collateral rules. Existing accepted
inputs may avoid changes; a new receipt needs compatible onboarding or an upgrade. Direct delivery of
existing pDAI can supply offers or eligible reserves without an issuer detour. FEI and Synthetix
conversions are optional branches when they improve net output or distribution. FEI receives a worked
example because its local one-for-one conversion is clearly demonstrated; it links FEI to pDAI units,
rather than independently anchoring either to dollars. The saved Synthetix evidence also connects
native PLS purchases of pDAI, wrapper issuance of sUSD and funded market outputs; these mixed-
position flows are not one isolated profitable cycle or fresh L2 delivery.
Each arrow needs its asset, effective executor, payer, obligations and timing. Attestations authenticate
state or delivery; issuance creates claims; a funded market supplies the paid asset. A successful local
cycle validates local circulation. Fresh L2 financing additionally needs its accepted delivery and source
obligations; instructions can coordinate spending without supplying assets. Copied Arbitrum authority
does not confer Optimism/Synthetix permissions. The control audit (Appendix 52) preserves those
distinctions.
3. Aave and Portal can advance local claims
Aave is the lending and receipt layer; Portal is its V3 destination-credit branch. Ordinary
supply deposits underlying and creates its aT oken. Borrowing draws available reserve cash and creates
debt. Portal lets an authorized Bridge caller issue the recognized destination aT oken before matching
underlying arrives. Source authentication belongs to the adapter; Aave checks local permission and
reserve validation. This is the credit concept in Aave's Portal proposal.

5. Common accounting directs connected market
arbitrage
The policy admits specific tokens, normalizations, conversion rights, limits and suspension conditions.
Common U compares opportunities; actual fees, basket rules, slippage and available payment assets
determine execution. Funded conversions transmit support through the eligible connected markets in
each usable direction. Fees, capacity and delays determine the achievable relative-price bands; one
working mint does not establish the reverse route or every AMM quote.
Buy a cheap eligible coin, convert through an accepting issuer and obtain a coin scarce elsewhere. Or
buy a cheap issuer coin and redeem its funded underlying. Authorized issuance or removal of supply can
extend those operations. Under the restoration interpretation, the objective is to improve connected
liquidity while acquiring useful assets; each individual trade need not profit.
Curve connects OUSD, mUSD and other metacoins to pDAI/pUSDC/pUSDT through 3CRV; Reserve eUSD
uses FRAXBP . Balancer and lending venues provide further eligible paths. Shared base reserves count
once: multiple issuer routes using the same 3pool or FRAXBP cash are not independently funded
alternatives. Rebalancing one venue must account for the payment resources and obligations left in the
others. Selling newly issued tokens into a pool consumes counterassets; reverse trades, funded
redemption or contraction, or new inputs must restore the needed capacity.
FEI has a demonstrated one-for-one pDAI conversion. Historical mUSD and post-shutdown sDAI cycles
closed with 200,053.199510 PLS and 110.687385 PLS after gas. These usable proceeds could
finance later operations; their subsequent deployment is a separate connection to establish. Profit and
direct price support are distinct jobs: the actual sDAI cycle ended by selling pDAI and slightly lowering its
closing pool's PLS/pDAI ratio. Under coordinated intent, its proceeds could support a different venue. The
policy must assess complete closing flows. The closed-trade reconciliation (Appendix 25) records the
actual endpoints.
Supply buffers differ by implementation. The checked PWRD/STBT pools use live balances; OUSD, UZD
and Lybra have different treatment. Rebases, minting, borrowing and income require separate resource
accounting. The rebase audit (Appendix 36) preserves these distinctions.
6. Build support gradually and keep pDAI circulating
The proposed construction has five phases. They can overlap; selected routes become usable before the
whole network is commissioned.

The acquisition assumption is a consistent allocation every ten seconds while pDAI is below target and

Acquiring a finite seller cohort can reduce its remaining inventory. Liquidity allocation and lending can

Target-price sales are the replenishment phase of the acquisition strategy. Buyers receive pDAI
while the network receives payment assets that can fund subsequent support. The policy also routes
available pDAI into measured shortages across connected pools, lending reserves and compatible
issuers. Releasing supply at the target can serve demand and contain a premium while restoring useful

A funded offer at the target also creates a distribution incentive: where another venue pays a premium

budget the other base assets and shared reserves alongside the pDAI refill.
A direct sale to a user restores the seller's payment resources. Its further allocation determines which
pool or lending reserve is refilled. Conversely, a user buying pDAI from 3pool removes DAI while adding
the input stablecoin. The proposed network closes that loop by supplying pDAI where routed demand
removes it and directing recovered resources to the next support requirement. The aim is repeated
redistribution across the ecosystem, with each shortage and funded refill recorded.

Proceeds allocated to backing, earning positions or other venues also compete with payment capacity

across wallets. Renewed selling still requires timely inputs, and lending can return pDAI through
withdrawals or borrow-and-sell activity. More aT okens than pT okens provides support through permitted

Universal fixed Ethereum redemption is not required for the bounded local policy. External access still

variable exchange rates and require separate deployment, reserves and bridge evidence.
